name: Hash-ribbon miner-capitulation rebound long (BTC, 1d)
rationale: ECONOMIC MECHANISM: miners are structurally forced sellers. When price falls below the all-in cost of high-cost rigs, those rigs power off and network hashrate rolls over; a low current hashrate reading (below a fitted floor) marks the supply-side exhaustion of the marginal forced seller. Buying here takes the other side of capitulating miners liquidating balance sheets and gets paid over weeks as the distressed flow clears. VanEck/CoinMetrics 2025: negative hashrate-growth episodes preceded positive 180d BTC returns ~77% of the time. Persists because miner cost curves are physical (energy + hardware ROI now >1000 days), not arbitraged away by a published signal. Entry: btc_hashrate below a fitted floor (miners capitulating) AND price washed out (bb_z below a fitted floor). Exit: RSI recovers through a fitted ceiling (rebound underway) or stop/TP/time. DISCONFIRMER 1: if a plain bb_z washout dip-buy on price alone matches the deflated Sharpe, the hashrate feature adds nothing and this dies. DISCONFIRMER 2: the 77% stat is halving-cycle survivorship — kill if the edge collapses post-2023. DISCONFIRMER 3: median hold >30d makes it a slow TAA sleeve not a snipe. Must clear DSR>=0.95, maxDD<=25%, net of fees.
catalyst: miner hashrate capitulation into a washed-out BTC price
